question.prompt: How many factors of \(2020\) have more than \(3\) factors? (As an example, \(12\) has \(6\) factors, namely \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(6,\) and \(12.\))

solutions.explanation:
Factor \(2020\) to organize its divisors:

\[
2020=2^2\cdot5\cdot101.
\]

Every divisor has the form \(2^a5^b101^c\), where \(a\) is \(0,1,\) or \(2\), while \(b\) and \(c\) are each \(0\) or \(1\). These choices give \(3\cdot2\cdot2=12\) different divisors.

Which have at most three factors of their own? The number \(1\) has one factor. The primes \(2,5,101\) each have two, and \(4\) has three: \(1,2,4\).

Every remaining divisor contains two distinct primes, say \(p,q\), so it has at least the four different factors \(1,p,q,pq\). Thus the five numbers just listed are the only exceptions.

There are \(12-5=\boxed{7}\) qualifying factors, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). First organize the factors of \(2020\), then ask how many factors each of those numbers has.
solutions.title: Use the prime factorization to count divisors and remove the exceptions
